title: Design futures
description: An audit of the site and its design system, and where each part could go next.

paragraphs:
Design futures
11 November 2026

This is an audit of the site and its design system, followed by four reports that propose where each part could go next. Every proposal is built as a working prototype from the existing tokens and Edit components, and embedded in the shared demo frame so you can use it rather than imagine it.
The reports: Editor panels, Page blocks, Components and Page layouts.

The engine source, the repository docs, the open issues, the live pages in View and in Edit, and the Design System page of the Figma file. For Figma I read the page structure and the Tokens, Atom Variants, Dev Panel Contents and Dev Panels sections; I did not open every nested component.

The reports themselves are documents in the page-block schema, rendered by the same block renderer as any write-up. They live in src/reports in the engine repository because routine content is private and yours to author, and nothing links to them, so the production build prunes them.

It is unusually coherent. One spacing unit is derived from the body type and everything hangs off it. Colour is three tiers of tokens with a written role for each ink. Edit chrome is monochrome on purpose, with amber on a single warning icon as its one colour. A dashed hairline means editable and nothing else. Motion fades and rises but does not pop.

The parts that carry the personality are small and specific: the segmented control whose two edges ride separate springs, the gap pill that freezes while you choose, the field whose edge fades follow the caret. The proposals try to add things of that kind, and to avoid adding anything that would need a new colour, a new radius or a new shadow.
Four pressures come out of the product vision and the issue list, and each report leans on them.

Controls move onto the page. The vision calls pop-up tuners a current means, not the destination. Seventeen panel titles are registered today, and the image tools alone are about 3,500 lines of tuner.
Edit goes online, at full parity. That means a phone. A 352px floating panel that you drag by its title bar has no equivalent on a touch screen yet.

Build in public, for yourself. Open-sourcing the engine and blocks makes the work visible and gives other people a place to fork it. The point is to document what I am making and explore ideas that interest me, with useful additions from forks able to find their way back into the main repo.
Pages need to be skimmed. Several open issues are about a case study reading in a few scrolls, and text, titles and images are about two thirds of every block in use.

Make the site unmistakably mine. The next design work is the homepage: a material, physical-product point of view that is legible in the first few seconds. The current veil and cursor demo are useful placeholders while that direction develops.

Width docs have drifted. interface-conventions.md and page-width.md both give the text column as 40em. global.css ships 37.5em. The sidebar threshold derived from it is still correct because it reads the media column.

Panel names differ between Figma and code. Figma has Gallery manager and Project settings; code and the UI say Pages and Page settings. Figma has no frames for Video, Add image, New project or the award sizers.

The save bar restyles buttons itself. saveBar.css redefines padding, radius and fills for every button inside it and has its own filled class, so a Button with emphasis="filled" placed in the bar renders as a ghost. I hit this building the change ledger. It is the same drift the button plan describes, in the one place that plan does not list.
There is no slider. Numeric settings are selects of preset steps. #134 already asks for one, and three of the proposals here need it.
Per-viewport overrides are invisible. Panels switch between Desktop, Tablet and Mobile, but nothing shows which viewport has its own value or where an inherited one comes from.

Dark mode is half a system. The dark token set exists and Figma has a Dark frame, but #transition-overlay is a literal white, DemoLayout pins data-theme="light", and #137 is open on the demo frame. I kept every prototype on semantic tokens so they follow the theme when it lands.

Dev stale-style trap. Editing a layout’s scoped style in a running review preview served the old stylesheet until I restarted it, exactly as dev-authoring.md warns. New prototype routes also needed a restart to appear.

Each proposal says what exists, what I would change and why, then shows it. The prototypes are real DOM built from Button, SegmentedControl, DevPanel, Menu, ToggleRow, TextField, Badge and Hairline, plus the tokens. Where I needed something the system lacks, that gap is itself a proposal in the Components report.
They are prototypes. None of them writes content, and none is wired into Edit. The layout you are reading is the one real change: a write-up with the docs’ On this page rail borrowed into its gutter.
